reports.title: Zscaler Announces First Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 20% to $949.3m and adjusted EPS of $1.23, both above estimates; agreed to be bought by CrowdStrike, guidance withdrawn

other.label: Free cash flow
other.change: 44% of revenue, vs 52% a year ago

results: Revenue grew 20% to $949.3m, above the $938.2m estimate; adjusted EPS of $1.23 beat the $1.16 estimate.
ARR rose 21% to $3.88bn; net new ARR was $111m.
Adjusted operating margin improved to 24.3% from 21.8%, but on a GAAP basis the net loss widened to $27.4m, mainly on a higher tax charge.
Operating cash flow was a record $541.0m and free cash flow $416.5m; capex jumped to $106.9m from $17.3m.
Zscaler agreed to be acquired by CrowdStrike in an all-stock deal: 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

guidance.summary: Because of the CrowdStrike deal, Zscaler withdrew its earlier financial guidance and will not give new guidance.

points: No results call was held: the company cancelled it because of the CrowdStrike deal.
In the release, CEO Jay Chaudhry said AI is pushing firms to rethink security and called the quarter a strong start.
The deal values Zscaler at about $260.41 a share, a 34% premium to the 20 Nov close, and about $43.9bn in enterprise value.
Chaudhry and affiliates, holding about 34% of the shares, have agreed to vote for the deal; closing needs shareholder and regulatory approval.
Closing is expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028; the two firms run independently until then.
call.source: No call held; based on the press release (Exhibit 99.1) and the deal announcement filed by Zscaler

watch: Progress on shareholder and regulatory approvals for the CrowdStrike deal.
The CrowdStrike share price, which sets the value Zscaler holders receive.
Whether ARR growth and cash flow hold up while the deal is pending.
